title: fix(plugin-timeline,types): a gantt-variant timeline draws a date-only end through the end of that day (objectui#11112)
body:
Fixes #11112
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

A `variant: 'gantt'` timeline read every date through `readGanttDate` (objectui#10866), which puts a date-only value at local midnight of its day: the START of the day. The bar was drawn to that instant, so:

- **An inclusive end drew one day short.** Measured on the base `db11afd49` with the schema catalog's `gantt-style-timeline.json` (the named producer): API Design, `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-31`, ended at `24.793%` of the axis while the February column began at `25.620%` (30 versus 31 of the 121 days).
- **A same-day task drew zero wide.** A bar whose date-only start and end name one day measured `width: 0%`.

## What this changes (triage `5893731138`: a date-only end is inclusive)

- **One end read: `readGanttBarEnd`.** It reads the value through `readGanttDate` exactly as a start is read, and then, for a date-only value only, steps to the next local midnight with the day column's own step (`DAY_AXIS.step`). "Date-only" is decided by the predicate `toDisplayDate` and `plugin-gantt` already ask, `isRealCalendarDate` from `@object-ui/core`. No new regex. A value with a time part, a number or a `Date` is an instant, and the bar ends at it, per objectui#10866.
- **The bar geometry takes it.** `calculateBarDimensions` places a bar from `readGanttDate(start)` to `readGanttBarEnd(end)`. The catalog's API Design now ends exactly where the February column begins, and a same-day bar is one day wide. Across a DST change, that day's column is 23 or 25 hours wide, and so is the bar.
- **The computed extent takes the same end.** `calculateDateRange` now also returns `through`, the last instant any bar covers, with each end read by `readGanttBarEnd`. `timelineAxis` runs on to the unit that contains it. The printed `minDate` / `maxDate` are unchanged, and so is the inverted-range diagnostic's wording. On `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter` and `year`, a unit that contains a day already contains every instant of it, so no scale gains a column. It matters on `hour`: the computed `maxDate` is a day, which an hour axis read as that day's first hour. A pinned `maxDate` stays exactly the author's range, and the empty plan's one-unit axis (objectui#6750) is untouched.
- **The end label is unchanged.** `formatDate` still prints the authored end day in the tooltip.
- **Declared.** `TimelineGanttItemBar.endDate` in `packages/types/src/data-display.ts` says "Inclusive for a date-only value", and its zod twin's `.describe()` in `packages/types/src/zod/data-display.zod.ts` says the same. The accept set is unchanged.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/plugins/plugin-timeline.mdx` states the rule under "Gantt Item". Its gantt example's Mockups bar was `2024-01-15` to `2024-02-01`, the day Development starts, so it now ends on `2024-01-31`.
- One changeset: `@object-ui/plugin-timeline` and `@object-ui/types`, patch.

## `plugin-gantt`'s own date-only end convention (read before changing, as the triage asked)

It **differs**. `plugin-gantt` has no end-specific rule, and its effective reading is **exclusive**, a half-open `[start, end)`:

- `readTaskDate` in `ObjectGantt.tsx` reads a date-only end like a start, at local midnight of the named day. This is pinned by `ObjectGantt.noSchemaZone-10866.test.tsx`: "a stored `2026-10-05` → `2026-10-09` reads as those days at local midnight".
- `GanttView`'s `styleFor` draws the bar to `dateToX(end)`, with a one-unit minimum width. So a same-day task shows one day wide, but a January 1st to 31st task is 30 days wide.
- `scheduling.ts` documents "The (exclusive) end instant", with finish-to-start as `B.start >= A.end`.
- The drag write-back (`toStoredDateValue`) writes the day at the bar's right edge.
- The tooltip's duration is `round((end - start) / day)`.

Its catalog producers still author inclusive ends: `project-timeline-with-dependencies.json` has `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-15`, with the successor starting `2024-01-16`. So under the inclusive reading, `plugin-gantt` draws them one day short with a one-day gap.

⛔ This PR does not change `plugin-gantt`. The question of making the two gantt surfaces agree in one place is raised in the dev report on this card, with options.

## In-place fix, named (bounded: same defect class, same file, same gate family)

The `through` extent also repairs an existing `hour`-axis overrun for instant ends. Measured on the base: one bar from `2026-10-05T09:00:00` to `12:00:00` on `scale: 'hour'` drew a one-column axis (`Oct 5, 12 AM`) with the bar at `left: 900%; width: 300%`. The computed `maxDate` was printed as a day and lost its hour. It now draws 12 columns and the bar ends at `100%`. This is the same mechanism the inclusive end needed on `hour`: without it, a date-only bar on an hour axis would have run to `192%`.

## Pins

New file `TimelineGantt.inclusiveEnd-11112.test.tsx`, next to the objectui#11079 axis pins:

- **The catalog, read from disk.** Each bar ending on a month's last day ends exactly at that month column's edge (API Design, Implementation, QA Phase at `100%`). The mid-month ends run through their day. The tooltip still names the authored end.
- **A same-day date-only bar is one day wide.** This holds on a day axis (its column), on a one-day plan, and on a month axis (1 of 31).
- **Instants keep their instant.** This covers an ISO date-time at midnight (with the date-only spelling of the same day as a control), a mid-day date-time, an epoch number and a `Date`.
- **The computed axis reaches where the bars are drawn.** An hour axis over date-only bars gives the last day 24 columns. An hour axis over an instant end ends at that hour. A month axis gains no column.

In `TimelineGantt.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`, run under Los Angeles and Shanghai by the objectui#10866 zone-pin driver:

- The producer's API Design bar ends where February begins in both zones.
- The `PINNED_MIXED` instant bar's end is unchanged. This is the card's "a datetime end is unchanged" pin.
- The DST case's bar now starts and ends on March 8th, and is exactly the 23-hour column.

## Re-derived pins (fixture triage)

These pins spelled a one-unit bar with an exclusive end, or held full-float widths over date-only ends. None of them pinned the exclusive reading as a rule.

- `TimelineGantt.oneAxis-11079.test.tsx`: the scale cases gain `e1` / `e2`, each unit's last day as authored. The `hour` scale keeps its instants, and the assertions are unchanged. The card's own day axis keeps its items, and its widths are re-derived (two days each).
- `TimelineGantt.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`: `COMPUTED` and `PINNED_MIXED` widths are re-derived.
- The full-float bar geometry pins in `timeline-gantt-empty-items.test.tsx` (#6750 pins 4 and 5b), `timeline-gantt-date-type-rule-6781.test.tsx` (pins 4 and 6), `timeline-gantt-null-date-6770.test.tsx` (pins 2 and 4) and `timeline-gantt-unusable-date-range.test.tsx` (pins 2 and 6) each gain one day per date-only end. The fixtures are unchanged, and each comment says why. The #6750 same-day pin now reads one day of May, where objectui#11079 drew it zero wide.

## Ablation (from the committed state, through `ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven)

Mutations ran on `renderer.tsx` at `9b7f949ab` against the new pin file. The subject resolves to source (`../renderer`), so no build was involved.

- **A1**, `DAY_AXIS.step(end);` deleted from `readGanttBarEnd` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `337a612a` → `243097ec`): **8 failed, 5 passed** of 13. The five that stay green are the fixture-on-disk case, the tooltip case, and the instant cases.
- **A2**, `through` not passed to the axis (anchor 1 → 0, replacement 0 → 1, blob → `18860d8d`): **2 failed, 11 passed**. The two are exactly the two hour-axis cases.
- **Restored**: 13 passed. The blob equals the HEAD blob `337a612a`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Verification

Final head `2d26d3b76`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-timeline/`: 38 files passed, 402 tests passed, 34 skipped. The skipped cases are the zone cases, which run only under the driver.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-timeline type-check`: exit 0. It covers `tsconfig.test.json`, so it includes the tests.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the ten changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files: 0 errors. The warning count per file is identical to the base (`--stdin` on the base blobs), so the diff adds none.

At `9b7f949ab`. Nothing under `packages/types/` and none of the zone pin files changed after it, and `git diff 9b7f949ab..2d26d3b76` names only three plugin-timeline test files:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`: 282 files, 6491 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`: exit 0.
- The dependency closure `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-timeline^...' build`: exit 0.
- `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts`: 27 passed. Each pin file ran every case in both zones.

Gates, all exit 0 at `2d26d3b76`:

- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-doc-fence-languages`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-doc-component-types`.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test`: NOT GOVERNED.

NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples`. The reason: both refuse without a scoped 34-package build (PREREQUISITE, exit 2). The docs edit is one string literal in a typed example, plus prose. CI runs both.

## Acceptance notes

- I read the pending `11079-timeline-one-axis.md` by hand. It names no file this change touches, so `check-changeset-claims` does not list it. Its sentence "a task that starts and ends at the same instant is a zero-width bar" still holds for instants. A date-only same-day task is now one day wide, and this PR's changeset says so. The pending note is not edited.
- `check-changeset-claims` lists 13 pending changesets that name `data-display.ts` or `data-display.zod.ts`. Each one is about another key. This change edits only the `endDate` doc text in those files, so none of them is falsified.
- The zod `.describe()` wording is not pinned by a test. No consumer parses it, and it mirrors the TypeScript docblock.
